Tests for a Semi-Parametric Model

Source: R/semireg-anova.R
anova.semireg.Rd

Tests of the fixed effects and of the smooth terms of a semireg or semireg_tmb fit, with the package's own code (no lmerTest needed).

Arguments

object

A semireg or semireg_tmb fit.

type

"III" (default) or "II": the type of the tests of the fixed effects.

smooth

Logical: test the smooth terms (refits the model once per smooth block)? The default is TRUE.

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class "pm_semi_anova" with fixed (the table of the fixed effects) and smooth (a data frame: the variance of each smooth block, the log-likelihoods of the model with and without it, the likelihood ratio statistic, its p-value and the reference distribution), printed together.

Details

Fixed effects: Type III (or II) tests from pm_anova(): for gaussian fits Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df and the adjusted covariance (the df equal those of the same model fitted by nlme::lme); for generalized fits Wald chi-square tests. The fixed parts of the smooths (e.g. x and f:x for s(x, by = f)) are tested here: they are the straight-line parts of the curves.

Smooth terms: for each block of smooth random effects (one variance), the likelihood ratio test of the variance being zero, i.e. of the curve being its straight-line part: the model is refitted without the block (with the same fixed effects, so REML likelihoods can be compared for gaussian fits). The tests are those of varcomp(fit, test = TRUE): as the variance is on the boundary of its range under the null hypothesis, the reference is the mixture \(\frac12\chi^2_0 + \frac12\chi^2_1\) (Self and Liang, 1987), and for the only random effect of a gaussian fit the exact null distribution of the restricted likelihood ratio (Crainiceanu and Ruppert, 2004), where the mixture is conservative; lmerTest::ranova() used the full chi-square, more conservative still. Column test names the distribution. For an s(x, f) smooth the block of the deviation curves tests whether the curves of the levels of f have the same shape. For small samples permlmer or bootmodels on fit$semer give resampling tests.

References

Crainiceanu, C. M. and Ruppert, D. (2004). Likelihood ratio tests in linear mixed models with one variance component. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 66, 165-185.

Self, S. G. and Liang, K.-Y. (1987). Asymptotic properties of maximum likelihood estimators and likelihood ratio tests under nonstandard conditions. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 82, 605-610.

Examples

library(predictmeans)
data(Dialyzer, package = "nlme")
fm <- semireg(rate ~ s(pressure, QB, k = 6) + (1 | Subject), data = Dialyzer, prt = FALSE)
anova(fm)
#> Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df)
#> 
#> Response: rate
#>                    F Df  Df.res  Pr(>F)    
#> (Intercept)   6.5438  1 116.395 0.01181 *  
#> pressure    183.8452  1 109.641 < 2e-16 ***
#> QB            6.8948  1  33.301 0.01296 *  
#> pressure:QB 219.5102  1 114.064 < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Smooth terms: likelihood ratio tests of variance = 0 (the curve is its straight-line part);
#> reference: exact restricted LRT for the only random effect of a gaussian fit, otherwise 0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1)
#>           term variance logLik logLik.without   LRT  p.value
#>     s_pressure      176 -361.9         -368.4 13.06 0.000151
#>  s_pressure_QB        0 -361.9         -361.9  0.00 1.000000
#>                       test
#>  0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1)
#>  0.5 chi2(0) + 0.5 chi2(1)
